practices.practice: Create and reuse a single process-wide MongoClient (singleton) rather than opening a new client per request and keep it open for the app lifetime.
Always require TLS on the wire (tls=true/ssl=true) and use SCRAM-SHA-256 authentication in production connection strings.
Prefer PyMongo's AsyncMongoClient for Python async code (newer async API) rather than Motor; create one AsyncMongoClient and reuse it across the process.
Design compound indexes using the ESR rule (Equality → Sort → Range); for moving-average queries prefer a compound index like {patientId:1, testCode:1, timestamp:1}.
Use TTL indexes to automatically expire time-series documents but be aware TTL requires a Date field, cannot be compound, and expiry is not instant (background sweeper runs ~60s).
Push $match and $sort stages before $setWindowFields, include allowDiskUse:true for memory-heavy aggregations, and use explain("executionStats") to confirm index usage and avoid COLLSCAN.

Use change streams for real-time alerts and persist resume tokens (resumeAfter / startAtOperationTime) so listeners can recover from restarts; use startAtOperationTime or historical replay when supported to recover older events.

practices.practice: Do not store DOCUMENTDB_URI or other secrets in source control; read the connection string from environment variables or a secret store (Azure Key Vault) and prefer managed identity / Entra RBAC in production.
When using change streams at scale, parallelize by physical-shard resume tokens (one watcher per token) to avoid single-thread hotspots and to ensure complete coverage of each physical partition.

practices.practice: Choose a partition (shard) key with high cardinality and even distribution (write-heavy workloads) or the most-common query filter (read-heavy workloads) to avoid hot partitions; test with representative load.

Azure DocumentDB often recommends setting retryWrites=false in connection strings for compatibility; drivers should still use retryable reads where supported and application-level retries should be idempotent with exponential backoff for transient errors and throttling (429).

practices.practice: Use provider monitoring and diagnostic settings (slow-query logs, metrics for CPU/memory/IOPS/connections) and alert on sustained throttling or long-running aggregations.

Vector indexes in Azure DocumentDB use `cosmosSearch`; pick the engine (DiskANN/HNSW/IVF) by scale, store normalized vectors for cosine similarity, and tune index/query parameters (lBuild, lSearch, maxDegree) to trade recall vs latency.

When building or deploying a cluster, size compute/IOPS (and enable autoscale if helpful) to handle ingestion spikes and aggregation workloads; monitor RU consumption and plan partitioning to avoid RU storms from hot partitions.
Secure network access by using Private Endpoints and firewall rules and grant the application least-privilege users/roles instead of embedding full-admin credentials.

Design time-series ingestion models (bucketed documents versus one-document-per-sample) according to ingest rate: use bucketed documents to reduce index pressure at very high ingest rates and use per-sample documents for moderate ingestion to simplify queries.
Make seed and demo scripts idempotent and include environment guards to avoid accidental runs against production; never embed production credentials in scripts.
Log operational events (index creation, explain plans, change-stream errors) and capture slow-query samples, but never log secrets or connection strings.
Use server-side schema validation or application-level validation (Beanie / Pydantic) to ensure documents include required fields and correct types for critical collections.

practices.practice: Do not rely solely on TTL for recovery or compliance; ensure you have provider backups and a documented retention/restore policy so expired or deleted data can be recovered when needed.
When using vector search, store vector metadata (model name, dimensionality) alongside vectors and limit vector dimensionality to what the chosen index/engine supports.
Use per-collection index budgets (keep 5–15 useful indexes) and run $indexStats to detect unused indexes and hide/drop them safely during low-traffic windows.
Transactions across multiple partitions are expensive; avoid multi-partition transactions for high-throughput ingestion and, if transactions are needed, keep them single-partition and short-lived.

practices.practice: When the driver or server must be compatible with used features (e.g., $setWindowFields, change streams, vector search), verify driver and server wire-protocol/feature support and fail fast if incompatible.
Precompute boolean alert flags (e.g., isCritical) and add an index on them if you need low-latency alert queries rather than scanning recent documents each time.

Avoid creating a new MongoClient per request when using serverless platforms; initialize the client at module scope so it survives warm invocations and set pool sizes appropriate to function concurrency.

When the service does not support server-side retryable writes, set retryWrites=false in the connection string and rely on safe, idempotent application-level retries with backoff for transient faults instead.

When running change-stream listeners, checkpoint progress (durably store resume tokens) and keep one watcher per resume token (one thread/process per physical partition) to avoid losing events on crashes.

Use explain('executionStats') to verify that your compound index is actually used by aggregation queries (keysExamined / docsExamined close to nReturned) and avoid blocking SORT stages by matching index prefixes.
When deploying production clusters, use Key Vault references for admin passwords and avoid including credentials in template parameter files or committed configs.

practices.practice: PRIOR_K04: Azure DocumentDB maps/controls consistency itself and ignores client-specified writeConcern (writes are quorum/mapped to account consistency); do not rely on setting writeConcern on the client to achieve provider-level durability semantics.
